about.title: Trinidad Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Trinidad may be a small coastal community in Humboldt County, but residents and visitors here rely on the same consumer products as anyone else — vehicles traveling US-101, marine and fishing equipment used near the harbor, tools, appliances, and outdoor gear suited to the rugged terrain around Patricks Point Drive and Trinidad Frontage Road. When one of these products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can be serious and unexpected. California law generally allows injured people to pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer without having to prove carelessness, since strict liability applies to many defective-product cases. If a product hurt you or someone in your household in Trinidad, keeping the item exactly as it was at the time of injury matters. LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who evaluates product liability claims and works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Trinidad Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often allows defective-product claims under strict liability, meaning you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the pool of parties an attorney can pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because the physical product is often central evidence in a defect claim, an attorney can advise you early on how to store and protect it before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving negligence. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, if possible, and avoid repairs or alterations. This is especially relevant in a place like Trinidad, where outdoor and marine gear used along Patricks Point Drive or near the coast can be an important piece of evidence. An attorney can advise on proper storage until it's reviewed.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney in the network. Attorneys typically work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
